correctness.rationale: Multiplication has no base points and takes the product of projective factor spaces to a closed, diagonally invariant image. For B>d the monomial weights have distinct base-B digits, giving only monomial fixed points. Literally divide the d variable occurrences of each monomial into blocks of sizes d_i to see that every one of the binomial(d+m-1,m-1) fixed points is in the image. Localization does not require smoothness. Concretely, stratify by the support of the monomial coordinates. In a support of size at least two, divide by one nonzero coordinate to identify the ambient stratum with a torus. The nonzero vector of weight differences defines a one-dimensional subtorus; an integral torus coordinate change sends its primitive direction to the first coordinate. The corresponding invariant stratum of the image is the product of C* with its slice at first coordinate 1, so it has compactly supported Euler characteristic zero. Singleton supports contribute one each. Additivity and compactness give the ordinary Euler characteristic asserted. Over C the binary case is the entire space. For m>=3 the image is proper: x_0^(d-1)x_1+x_2^d is irreducible by primitivity and degree one in x_1. The conclusion does not concern the exact irreducible-factor stratum.
residual_risks: The unexecuted regression checker inspects finite weight, count and factorization cases only. No formal verification is credited; the proof covers the full range.

evidence: The arbitrary-partition spaces are projective multiplication images. For any closed invariant subset of projective space under a diagonal C* action of distinct weights, its Euler characteristic is the number of weight-coordinate points present; the support-stratum proof verifies this also for singular sets.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Localization covers all such invariant varieties, not just factorization loci. Every prescribed-degree multiplication image is invariant and contains all monomial coordinates.

value.rationale: The family and invariant are natural, and the equality for proper loci is a useful observation. But it follows mechanically from torus Euler localization plus the fact that monomials can be split into blocks of any sizes. The calculation detects no new structure of the partition-dependent strata, which it expressly does not address.
residual_risks: This decision does not extend to Euler characteristics of exact-factorization strata or refinements such as Betti numbers.
